why: Functions computed through special functions (incomplete gamma and beta, erfc, inverse distributions found by iteration) and least-squares fits. Excel and Cells both land within a few units of the 16th significant digit of the exact value (Cells checked against 50-digit mpmath when these were added), so the 15th digit can round either way. These agree with Excel to the relative difference given; anything beyond it fails.

families.why: For x ≥ 8 Excel's BESSELJ is up to about 2e-5 off the true value (BESSELJ(8.5,1) is -0.27311529 there, -0.27312196 exactly); Cells uses the Numerical Recipes asymptotic form, good to about 1e-9. Below 8 both use the same rational approximation and agree to the last digit.

Bond and loan sums: each cash flow is discounted and added, and Excel's order of operations isn't documented, so the last digit or two of these sums of many terms can differ (DDB loses digits to cancellation when salvage is near the book value).

Yields found by iteration: Excel stops its search once the price is within its tolerance, so its last digits are those of an unfinished iteration (agrees to 9 digits or better); ours iterates to the root.
